01 / ENVIRONMENT SYNTHESIS

Verifiable Environment Synthesis

We construct verifiable tasks and scale their environment states from v₀ to v₃ while keeping instructions, task logic, and tool schemas fixed.

02 / EXPERIMENTS

Experimental Results

We evaluate our models across MCPMark, MCP-Atlas, and Toolathlon-Verified, and further use LOCA-bench at 8k–64k environment-state sizes. Each reported pass rate averages four independent runs.

ProgAgent uses PTC evaluation; the baselines in the main results table use DTC. MCPMark excludes the GitHub suite. Toolathlon scores marked † are from the original Toolathlon benchmark; all other scores in that column are from Toolathlon-Verified. “–” denotes an unreported score.

On MCPMark, ProgAgent achieves average pass rates of 18.3% at 8B and 29.7% at 14B, respectively. On Toolathlon-Verified, ProgAgent reaches 9.3% at 8B and 17.1% at 14B, compared with at most 2.8% and 1.9% among the 8B and 14B baselines.

Moreover, on MCP-Atlas, ProgAgent-14B achieves 45.6%, comparable to Claude Sonnet-4.5 (43.8%) under the DTC harness. The gap is most pronounced on LOCA-bench: the evaluated comparable-size baselines score zero at 32k and 64k, while ProgAgent mitigates context rot to maintain pass rates between 17.3% and 30.7% at 64k.

Training-data Scales

The resulting 215 tasks are each instantiated at 4 scales, yielding a shared training pool of 860 task instances.

Training Paradigms across Benchmarks

The table below compares each training recipe with its untrained backbone under the same harness. For untrained backbones, switching to PTC provides limited benefits across benchmarks and often yields the lowest scores among the three harnesses. Training reverses this pattern: after SFT and RL, the PTC recipe achieves the highest aggregate score on each benchmark at both model scales.

ProgAgent-14B reaches 29.7% on MCPMark and 45.6% on MCP-Atlas, compared with 8.0% and 29.7% for DTC, respectively. ProgAgent-8B also outperforms the 8B DTC model on all four benchmarks.

The chart above compares the three training paradigms on LOCA-bench, showing gains from both SFT and RL. As the environment state scales, DTC suffers from context rot. In contrast, PTC effectively mitigates this degradation and sustains robust performance, achieving average pass rates of 24.3% (8B) and 38.3% (14B). Furthermore, despite providing a more flexible action space during both training and evaluation, the Hybrid paradigm performs worse than PTC.

03 / ANALYSIS

Analysis

Training dynamicsEnvironment scalingTool orchestrationRemaining challenges

What Does PTC Change During Training?

At 14B, DTC achieves substantially lower rewards than PTC and Hybrid. During RL training, tool-output tokens under PTC decrease by roughly 20%, falling below 20k per episode; both programmatic paradigms use roughly half as many tool calls as DTC.

The 8B backbone reproduces the same trend: PTC and Hybrid achieve higher rewards with fewer tool-output tokens and tool calls than DTC.

Does Environment State Scaling Help?

Environment state scaling improves PTC performance on LOCA-bench across both backbones. Restricting training to v₀ reduces average pass rates from 24.3% to 16.0% at 8B and from 38.3% to 23.7% at 14B.

How Does PTC Facilitate Tool Orchestration?

PTC models use loops, conditional execution, and error handling to orchestrate tools during RL. PTC-trained models outperform DTC-trained models under both evaluation interfaces, with a 11.9-percentage-point gain on MCP-Atlas at 14B under DTC evaluation.

What Challenges Remain for PTC Agents?

DTC-like behavior: on Playwright, 40.7% of ProgAgent-14B’s PTC calls contain a single tool invocation without control flow, error handling, or selective printing. Silent server failures: disabling server-level error detection reduces LOCA-bench pass rates from 24.3% to 19.3% at 8B and from 38.3% to 34.5% at 14B.

04 / PTC IN PRACTICE

Toolathlon-Verified: From an Emailed Schedule to Published Canvas Courses

This case shows how PTC uses loops and returned identifiers to coordinate dependent course-creation and configuration calls.

Instruction

This is admin3, a registrar from XXX University. The university has sent me the new semester's course schedule via email with the subject "Course Schedule Notification." I need you to help me find the courses I'm responsible for from the attached master schedule and create corresponding courses on Canvas for the instructors. The specific requirements are as follows:

  • Assign the corresponding instructor as the teacher for each course on Canvas. The instructors' emails are saved in my local workspace.
  • Publish an announcement for each course that includes the instructor's name and the class time.
  • If an instructor is teaching the same course multiple times, these courses should be set up for resource sharing in Canvas.
  • The syllabi for each course are saved in my workspace. Please publish them for their respective courses.
  • All courses I am responsible for need to be published.
AVAILABLE MCP SERVERS

Filesystem, Canvas, Terminal, Emails.

EXECUTION STEPS
Step 1 of 4
01

Select assigned courses and look up instructor IDs

PTC CALLPython
# data: parsed schedule rows (course, instructor, time, administrator).
# parse_tool_result: helper defined earlier to decode the tool response.
admin3_courses = [(c, i, t) for c, i, t, a in data if a == "admin3"]
instructor_map = {}
for name in set(i for _, i, _ in admin3_courses):
    result = tools["canvas_canvas_list_account_users"](
        account_id=account_id, search_term=name, page=1, per_page=20)
    users = parse_tool_result(result)
    if users:
        u = users[0] if isinstance(users, list) else users
        instructor_map[name] = u['id']
02

Create courses and use returned IDs to enroll instructors

PTC CALLPython
print(f"Processing {len(admin3_courses)} courses...")
created_courses = []
for idx, (course_name, instructor, class_time) in enumerate(admin3_courses):
    try:
        course = tools["canvas_canvas_create_course"](
            account_id=account_id, name=course_name,
            start_at=(date.today()).isoformat(),
            end_at=(date.today() + timedelta(days=365)).isoformat(),
            time_zone="America/Denver")
        course_id = course['id']
        tools["canvas_canvas_enroll_user"](
            course_id=course_id, user_id=instructor_map[instructor],
            role="TeacherEnrollment", enrollment_state="active")
        created_courses.append((course_name, course_id, instructor, class_time))
        print(f"[{idx+1}/{len(admin3_courses)}] Created {course_name} (ID={course_id}) for {instructor}")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"ERROR {idx}: {e}")
print(f"\nCreated {len(created_courses)} courses.")

04

Check selected course settings and summarize results

The following program checks course publication, teacher count, the public-syllabus flag, and announcement presence. Its success message refers to these checks; it does not verify instructor identity, syllabus or announcement content, or resource sharing.

PTC CALLPython
# courses: 27 course-name/ID pairs (literal list omitted).
# instructor_map: Canvas instructor IDs to names (dictionary omitted).
print("=== FINAL COMPREHENSIVE VERIFICATION ===\n")

# Track instructor-to-course count
instructor_courses = {}
for cname, cid in courses:
    detail = tools["canvas_canvas_get_course"](course_id=cid)
    tid = detail['teachers'][0]['id'] if detail['teachers'] else None
    if tid:
        instructor_courses.setdefault(tid, []).append(cname)

# Verify
all_ok = True
failures = []

for course_name, course_id in courses:
    detail = tools["canvas_canvas_get_course"](course_id=course_id)
    state_ok = detail['workflow_state'] == 'available'
    teacher_ok = len(detail['teachers']) == 1
    # Check teacher is correct
    actual_teacher = detail['teachers'][0]['display_name'] if detail['teachers'] else 'NONE'

    syll_ok = detail['public_syllabus']
    anns = tools["canvas_canvas_list_announcements"](course_id=course_id)
    ann_ok = len(anns) >= 1

    if not state_ok:
        failures.append(f"{course_name}: state={detail['workflow_state']}")
    if not teacher_ok:
        failures.append(f"{course_name}: teachers count={len(detail['teachers'])}")
    if not syll_ok:
        failures.append(f"{course_name}: syllabus not public")
    if not ann_ok:
        failures.append(f"{course_name}: no announcements")

    print(f"{course_name}: state={detail['workflow_state']}, teachers={len(detail['teachers'])} ({actual_teacher}), syll={syll_ok}, anns={len(anns)}")

if failures:
    print(f"\n✗ {len(failures)} failures: {failures}")
else:
    print(f"\n✓ All {len(courses)} courses verified successfully!")

# Instructor summary
print("\nInstructor-Course Mapping:")
for tid, cnames in sorted(instructor_courses.items()):
    print(f"  {tid} ({instructor_map[tid]}): {len(cnames)} courses - {cnames}")

print(f"\nTotal unique instructors: {len(instructor_courses)}")
print(f"Total courses: {len(courses)}")
